questions.instructions: A customer of an online electronics and home-goods shop wrote this message. Decide whether it describes an emergency.

criteria.true: The message describes a present or imminent danger to people or property.
criteria.false: The message describes an ordinary service issue with no danger to anyone.

questions.message: This sounds urgent, so I am connecting you with a colleague right now. If anyone is in danger, unplug the device if it is safe to do so and call 112.

questions.instructions: Rate how frustrated or upset the customer is in this message.
criteria: Frustrated: clearly annoyed, mentions repeated contact or delays
Angry: hostile wording, threatens to cancel, complain or leave a bad review
Furious: abusive, shouting, or threatening legal action
questions.message: I am sorry this has been so frustrating. I am bringing in a colleague who can sort this out with you directly.

questions.instructions: Classify what the customer's message is mainly about.
Decide whether the reply states a fact or makes a promise that the tool outcomes do not support.

criteria.true: The reply contains at least one claim or promise not backed by the tool outcomes.
criteria.false: Every fact and promise in the reply is backed by the tool outcomes.

questions.message: I want to be sure you get accurate information, so a colleague will check this and reply to you by email today.

questions.instructions: Decide whether the customer's own request explicitly asks for what this tool does.

criteria.true: The customer explicitly asked for this refund or return.
criteria.false: The customer did not ask for this refund or return.
